Class WindowSignals

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.window.WindowSignals
public final class WindowSignals extends Object
Which slot the cursor is over (hovered) and which slot was last clicked (selected), as Addresses, observed on the client. The ObservedReactions counterpart for interaction rather than content: both are client observers keyed by address through ClientSlotAddressing.

Keyed by address

A consumer asks about its own things, WindowSignals.isHovered(addr) or isSelected(addr), where addr is a panel or created-slot address it minted by id. It does not ask which vanilla index is hovered: addressing by identity makes a rule work the same in creative and survival, since a created slot has one address in both. MenuKitClient captures hover each client tick and selection on a screen click, clears the selection on close, and maps both through the shared addressing, so a hovered created slot reports its created address.

Client thread only.

  • Method Details

    • tickHover

      @Internal public static void tickHover(@Nullable net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu menu, @Nullable net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot hoveredSlot)
      Updates the hovered slot (MenuKitClient, each client tick). Null clears it. Only MenuKit's client tick writes the signals, from raw slots on the live screen. Consumers read them through isHovered(Address), hoveredName and the rest.

    • recordClick

      @Internal public static void recordClick(@Nullable net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu menu, @Nullable net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot clickedSlot)
      Records the last-clicked slot (MenuKitClient, on a screen click). Consumers read the selection through isSelected(Address) and selectedName.

    • clearSelection

      @Internal public static void clearSelection()
      Clears the selection (MenuKitClient, when a container screen closes). Only MenuKit calls it; consumers never reset the selection themselves.
